content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
Maester 3.0 supports Maester Packs. Two CISA packs live in their own repositories: maester365/maester-pack-scubagear (code SCUBA.M365, rows `MP.SCUBA.M365.MS.AAD.3.1` and so on, one per ScubaGear policy) and maester365/maester-pack-scubagoggles (code SCUBA.GWS, Google Workspace). Both are family tests whose instance source reads a ScubaResults file. Maester's built-in CISA suite (`tests/cisa`, framework file `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json`) already maps its tests to `cisa-scuba` requirements through the `Control` attribute. The goal is that ScubaGear pack rows can name the same requirements, so the framework view shows CISA's own result next to Maester's for each policy. ScubaGoggles has no framework file yet, so this mainly serves ScubaGear for now.

Task:
Let a family test's instances set their own `Control` (a framework requirement such as `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1`), so pack rows map to frameworks the way built-in tests do.

Today `Control` is resolved only during discovery: `Get-MtNativeTestInventory` (`powershell/internal/engine/Get-MtNativeTestInventory.ps1`, around line 160) calls `Resolve-MtTestBenchmark` (`powershell/internal/engine/Get-MtSuiteFramework.ps1`) to build `Benchmark` and add the requirement's `Related` references. Instances only exist at run time (`Expand-MtTestFamily` in `powershell/internal/engine/Invoke-MtNativePlan.ps1`). `Get-MtInstanceAttribute` (same file, around line 590) lets an instance set Product, RelatedProduct, Feature, Area, UserImpact, ImplementationCost and Mitre, but not Control.

Steps:
1. Accept `Control` on an instance (a string or a list of `<framework-key>:<id>` values). Resolve it when the family expands, with `Resolve-MtTestBenchmark` against the loaded frameworks (`Get-MtLoadedFramework` / `Get-MtFrameworkIndex`). The row gets its own `Benchmark`, and its `Control` gets the `Related` references. An unknown reference keeps the family's values, the same way the other instance attributes fall back.
2. Check how the HTML report and the framework/benchmark views group rows by requirement. When a pack row and a built-in test name the same requirement, show both under it; don't pick one.
3. Update the family docs (`website/docs/writing-tests/` and the pack docs in `website/docs/packs/writing-a-pack.md`) to list `Control` among the attributes an instance may set.
4. Add unit tests next to the existing instance-attribute tests, then run `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`. New `.ps1` files must be UTF-8 with a byte order mark (`FileEncoding.Tests.ps1`).

Done means a PR-ready branch with the change, its tests and the docs. Don't push or open a PR without asking.

function Set-MtTestFrameworkIndex {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Keeps the frameworks a family test's instances can name, by the test's file.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Discovery resolves a test's Control against the frameworks it can see (Get-MtFrameworkIndex): the ones
    shipped with Maester and those of the test's own suites. A family's instances exist only at run time, so
    Complete-MtNativeTest keeps that index here, and Get-MtTestFrameworkIndex returns it when an instance sets
    its own Control. A later discovery of the same file replaces it.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess = $false)]
    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSUseShouldProcessForStateChangingFunctions', '', Justification = 'Updates a module-scoped cache only.')]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $File,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [object] $Index
    )

    if ($null -eq $script:__MtTestFrameworkIndex) { $script:__MtTestFrameworkIndex = @{} }
    $script:__MtTestFrameworkIndex[$File] = $Index
}

function Get-MtTestFrameworkIndex {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns the frameworks a family instance's Control can refer to.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The index that discovery used for the family's own Control (Set-MtTestFrameworkIndex). A test that did not
    pass through discovery in this session, such as a row of the shipped catalogue, gets the frameworks shipped
    with Maester (Get-MtBuiltInFramework), which is what discovery gave it.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [object] $Test
    )

    $file = if ($Test -and $Test.PSObject.Properties['File']) { [string]$Test.File } else { $null }
    if ($file -and $script:__MtTestFrameworkIndex -and $script:__MtTestFrameworkIndex.ContainsKey($file)) { return $script:__MtTestFrameworkIndex[$file] }

    # Built once for the frameworks shipped with Maester, and again when those are read again.
    $null = Get-MtBuiltInFramework
    $builtIn = $script:__MtBuiltInFramework
    if (-not $script:__MtBuiltInFrameworkIndex -or -not [object]::ReferenceEquals($script:__MtBuiltInFrameworkIndex.Source, $builtIn)) {
        $script:__MtBuiltInFrameworkIndex = [pscustomobject]@{ Source = $builtIn; Index = Get-MtFrameworkIndex -WarningAction SilentlyContinue }
    }
    $script:__MtBuiltInFrameworkIndex.Index
}
EOF

## Tests and helpers

A pack's tests are [native tests](../writing-tests/index.mdx) with IDs `MP.<Code>.<n>`, or `MP.<Code>` for a family whose instances add their own part. (Packs that ship with
Maester are part of it and drop the `MP.`: the Zero Trust Assessment pack's tests are `ZTA.<n>`.) Every `.ps1` in a suite
or helper folder holds only functions: code outside a function is refused, because it would run while the pack
loads. A pack loads into a private module of its own, so its tests can call its helpers and Maester's exported
commands. One pack does not see another pack's functions unless it requires that pack and the pack lists them in
`Exports`. This keeps cooperating packs from colliding; it is not a security boundary, because code in the same
PowerShell process can reach anything in it (see [Pack security](./security.md)).

The scan flags, and raises the risk of, what a reviewer should look at: binary files, dynamic code
(`Invoke-Expression`, `[scriptblock]::Create`), starting processes, requests to hosts that `Uses.Network` does not
list, and module imports that `Uses.Modules` does not list.

## Showing a long-running test's output and progress

A test that runs a tool for a long time, such as an assessment in another PowerShell process, can show the person
running Maester what the tool is doing while it runs. In the full-screen dashboard both go into a box in the main
column; in the compact layout, CI and redirected output they are written to the console, indented.

- `Write-MtTestOutput` shows the tool's log. `-Title` opens the box, each line
  scrolls into it, `-Progress` pins a changing line at the bottom, and `-Complete` closes it (Maester closes it when
  the test ends).
- `Write-MtTestProgress` shows where the tool is, as a header at the top of
  the box: the stage (`-Stage`, `-StageNumber`, `-StageCount`), a bar of the items done (`-Completed`, `-Total`,
  `-Failed`, `-Running`), what it is working on (`-Current`, `-Status`), and the errors it reported
  (`-ErrorMessage`), which the box also counts. With `-Stages` (the names of all the stages) the stages are drawn
  as a track, like the phases of a Maester run. With `-Items` (each with `Id`, and optionally `Title`, `Status`,
  `Detail` and `Seconds`) the box lists the items running and those that finished, with their result and time,
  the way the dashboard lists Maester's own tests; outside the dashboard each finished item is written once. Each
  call replaces the progress before it, so pass everything you know each time; a call with only `-ErrorMessage`
  keeps the progress.
- When the tool runs tests of its own, `-Results` (`Passed`, `Failed`, `Error`, `Investigate`, `Skipped`,
  `Running`, `Total` and optionally `Name`) and `-Groups` (the same counts with a `Name` each, such as the pillars
  of an assessment, with `-GroupLabel 'Zero Trust Pillars'`) show them in the dashboard in place of Maester's own while the
  box is open: in the Results panel and the result blocks, and where the products are listed. The times of the
  items that finished go into the Pace graph next to the logo and the Slowest panel.

```powershell
Write-MtTestOutput -Title 'Collecting the tenant data'
Write-MtTestProgress -Stage 'Exporting' -StageNumber 1 -StageCount 3 -Completed 12 -Total 40 -Running 2 -Current 'Users', 'Groups'
Write-MtTestProgress -ErrorMessage 'The export of Devices failed: Forbidden'
```

A tool in another process does not need to call Maester to report its progress. Pipe its output to
`Write-MtTestOutput`, and have it write lines of this form to standard output, from any language:

```text
##maester[progress] {"stages":["Export","Tests","Report"],"stageNumber":1,"stage":"Exporting","completed":12,"total":40,"failed":1,"items":[{"id":"Users","detail":"page 3","seconds":12},{"id":"Groups","status":"Passed","seconds":4.2}]}
##maester[progress] {"stage":"Running tests","results":{"passed":80,"failed":12,"running":4,"total":300},"groupLabel":"Zero Trust Pillars","groups":[{"name":"Identity","passed":50,"failed":8,"total":120}]}
##maester[error] The export of Devices failed: Forbidden
```

These lines set the header instead of showing in the log. The JSON object takes the names of the parameters of
`Write-MtTestProgress` in any case (`error` for `-ErrorMessage`), and leaves out what it does not know. Write a
`progress` line when something changes (at most a few times a second): each one is drawn. A line that cannot be read is dropped.

The [Zero Trust Assessment pack](./zero-trust-assessment.md) is a worked example: its child process reads the
progress the assessment keeps and the progress logs it writes, once a second, and writes these lines (see
`Invoke-MtZtaCollection` in `packs/zero-trust-assessment/tests/Test.ZTA.ps1`).

#### What the result gets

Maester looks up each `Control` value of a test, in the order they are written. A value resolves when its key is
a framework that has a file and its ID is a requirement in that file.

- `Benchmark` is built from the first value that resolves: the `Framework`, its `Version`, the `Requirement` and
  the requirement's own facts. When no value resolves, `Benchmark` is `null`.
- `Control` holds the values the test wrote, followed by the `Related` references of every requirement that
  resolved, each once.

`Get-MtTest` shows both. See [the result schema](../result-schema.md#benchmark).

A framework is found by its key, whatever suite declares it. A custom test can name a framework that ships with
Maester (`cis-m365`, `cis-github`, `cisa-scuba`, `essential-eight`, `ism`) or one that a suite in your own test folder declares. Two suites
must not declare the same key: Maester warns, names both `suite.json` files and uses the first, and a framework
that ships with Maester comes before one of yours.

A `Control` value whose key no framework file has, such as `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)` or `iso-27001-2022:A.5.17`,
is written to the result as it is. It needs no file.

A problem with a framework never stops a run. Maester writes a warning that names the file and what is wrong:

- The file is missing or is not valid JSON, its `Framework` or `Version` differs from the `suite.json`, a
  requirement has no `Id` or an `Id` that is listed twice, or a `Related` reference is not written
  `<framework-key>:<control-id>`. No test gets a `Benchmark` or `Related` controls from that framework.
- A `Control` names a framework that has a file and a requirement that is not in it, usually a typing error. That
  value gives no `Benchmark`; the other tests keep theirs.

Family instances can now set their own `Control`, and each row gets its own `Benchmark` and the requirement's `Related` references, just like a built-in test. This is commit `637f98ee6` on branch `feat/instance-control`. It isn't pushed and there's no PR. The full unit suite (`./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`) passes: 7057 tests, no failures.

**How it works**
- **Engine** ([Invoke-MtNativePlan.ps1](powershell/internal/engine/Invoke-MtNativePlan.ps1)): `Get-MtInstanceAttribute` accepts `Control` as one value or a list. It lowercases the framework key and checks each value against the schema pattern, then resolves it with `Resolve-MtTestBenchmark`. The instance's values replace the family's `Control`.
- **Fallback**: a value that isn't written `<framework-key>:<id>`, or names a requirement the framework file doesn't have, is dropped. If nothing is left, the row keeps the family's `Control` and `Benchmark`.
- **Framework lookup**: instances only exist at run time, so discovery now keeps the framework list it used for each family test, by file (`Register-MtTestFrameworkIndex` in [Get-MtSuiteFramework.ps1](powershell/internal/engine/Get-MtSuiteFramework.ps1)). That means a pack instance can name `cisa-scuba` or a framework its own `suite.json` declares. A test read from the shipped catalogue uses the frameworks shipped with Maester, built once per session.

**Report**: no change was needed. The framework view and `Get-MtResultFramework` list every row that names a requirement, with no de-duplication. A ScubaGear row and the built-in CISA test for the same requirement therefore show up together under it.

**Docs**:
- [writing-tests/index.mdx](website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx): `Control` added to the table of instance properties, plus a note under "What the result gets".
- [writing-a-pack.md](website/docs/packs/writing-a-pack.md): a new "Mapping a pack's results to a framework" section with a ScubaGear-style example.

**Tests**: five new cases in [ReviewFixes.Tests.ps1](powershell/tests/functions/engine/ReviewFixes.Tests.ps1), next to the other instance-attribute tests:
- an instance's own `Benchmark` and `Related` references, with the family's values kept when an instance sets no `Control`;
- unknown or badly formed values falling back to the family's;
- a framework declared by the family's own `suite.json`;
- the shipped-framework fallback for catalogue tests.

None of this has been tried against the real ScubaGear pack.

## 📑 Description

A family test's instances can now set `Control` (one `<framework-key>:<id>` value or a list), so pack rows map to framework requirements the way built-in tests do. The motivating case is the ScubaGear pack (`maester365/maester-pack-scubagear`), whose rows are one per ScubaGear policy: each can now say `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`, and the framework view shows CISA's own result next to Maester's CISA test for the same requirement.

**Engine**
- `Get-MtInstanceAttribute` (in `Invoke-MtNativePlan.ps1`) accepts `Control`. It lowercases the framework key, checks each value against the schema pattern and resolves it with `Resolve-MtTestBenchmark`. The row gets its own `Benchmark`, and its `Control` gets the requirements' `Related` references. The instance's values replace the family's.
- Values that are malformed, or that name a requirement the framework file doesn't have, are dropped. If none are left, the row keeps the family's `Control` and `Benchmark`, the same fallback the other instance attributes use.
- Instances only exist at run time, so discovery now keeps the framework index it used for each family file (`Register-MtTestFrameworkIndex`). `Get-MtTestFrameworkIndex` returns it when an instance sets `Control`. As a result, a pack instance can name a shipped framework (`cisa-scuba`) or one declared in its own `suite.json`. A test read from the shipped catalogue uses the frameworks shipped with Maester, an index built once per session.

**Report:** no change needed. `model.ts` (`requirementsOf`, `requirementTests`) and `Get-MtResultFramework` already list every row that names a requirement, with no de-duplication. A pack row and a built-in test for the same requirement both appear under it.

**Docs:** `Control` added to the table of instance properties and to "What the result gets" in `writing-tests/index.mdx`, plus a new "Mapping a pack's results to a framework" section in `packs/writing-a-pack.md`.

## ℹ️ Additional Information

- New tests in `ReviewFixes.Tests.ps1` ("Family instances"):
  - an instance's own `Benchmark` and `Related` references;
  - no instance `Control`, so the family's values are kept;
  - unknown or badly formed values falling back to the family's;
